message.content: {"summary":"You present a strong, well-structured preliminary mission design, with a clear rationale, substantial orbital analysis, useful STK evidence and a conclusion that acknowledges limitations. To make the performance claims more persuasive, validate the downlink, regional coverage and 5 m imaging capability with complete engineering analyses rather than simplified estimates.","next_steps":["Complete an X-band link budget in Section 2.4, documenting antenna gains, transmit power, link margin and assumptions to demonstrate whether the 50 Mbit/s rate is achievable.","In Section 2.3, model coverage of the actual Great Barrier Reef area and account for off-nadir image quality; report validated coverage, revisit and mosaic-completion estimates.","In Section 2.1, support the 5 m imaging claim with detector sampling, optical performance, signal-to-noise and atmospheric analysis, then carry the validated performance and remaining caveats into your conclusion."],"criteria":{"C1":"Your Introduction clearly identifies the bleaching-imaging mission, its need, the single-spacecraft approach, AIMS as operator and the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority as a customer. Specific detail and citations support an accomplished response. To strengthen it further, qualify benefit claims carefully and connect them to evidence.","C2":"Sections 2.2–2.5 address launch choice, orbit and manoeuvres, ground access, mission duration and EOL. STK outputs and Appendix A provide useful design evidence. To strengthen this accomplished design, validate the 50 Mbit/s downlink, regional coverage estimates and 5 m imaging performance with complete engineering analyses.","C3":"Your Conclusion draws specific findings from the design and identifies four limitations, giving readers a suitably qualified takeaway. Keep this evidence-led approach, and update the conclusions as you validate the link budget, coverage and imaging-performance estimates.","C4":"The report has a logical engineering structure, concise Executive Summary, readable prose, labelled figures and tables, and in-text citations with a substantial bibliography. To make the presentation even more professional, refine minor stylistic awkwardness and complete bibliographic details consistently."}}
